payload.reason: The evidence indicates that regularization during fine-tuning can improve performance in the target domain without harming it, as shown by the combination of auxiliary penalty terms used in the study.

claims.text: Regularization of the fine-tuning process does not harm performance in the target domain and can improve it.
Combining different auxiliary penalty terms during fine-tuning leads to better performance in the target domain compared to methods that do not use regularization.
Fine-tuning improves target domain performance significantly compared to training from scratch, indicating that regularization is beneficial.
